selection: The four largest comparable loss forecasts verified in original film-trade reporting for 2026 releases, ranked by the highest quoted estimate. Eligible forecasts include post-theatrical income. This is a ranking of dated published forecasts found in the documented source review, not a complete ranking of actual losses.
ranking: Descending upper estimate; equal upper estimates share a rank. Ties are displayed by descending lower estimate, then title.
rangeMeaning: The envelope of the estimates explicitly quoted by each report, not a confidence interval or a calculation of gross minus budget.

rows.title: Digger

report.basis: Includes post-theatrical revenue; different insiders give different estimates.
report.assumption: The report expected worldwide box office not to exceed $40 million. Its other source made the loss dependent on premium video-on-demand performance.
report.caveat: The production budget is disputed. The Numbers lists $125 million; this loss report cites insiders at $163 million to $173 million. Current ticket sales have passed the report's $40 million assumption.
report.summary: Competing estimates depend partly on video-on-demand income.

rows.companies: Legendary Pictures, M. Productions, TC Productions, Warner Bros.

rows.title: Supergirl

report.basis: First-cycle loss forecast, including downstream income after cinemas.
report.assumption: Published after a $68 million worldwide opening. The report gives a $315 million worldwide break-even estimate, but does not specify the final worldwide gross assumed in its $125 million loss forecast.
report.caveat: This is Deadline's original June forecast, not an updated or audited loss. Variety's separate theatrical-only estimates are excluded from this comparison because they use a different revenue window.
report.summary: First-cycle estimate; no final-gross assumption was disclosed.

rows.companies: DC Studios, Domain Entertainment, Troll Court Entertainment, The Safran Company

rows.title: Moana

report.basis: First-cycle loss forecast, including revenue after cinemas.
report.assumption: The forecast assumed a final worldwide box office of $250 million.
report.caveat: Current worldwide ticket sales exceed the report's $250 million assumption. This is the original July forecast, not an updated loss estimate.
report.summary: The $250M worldwide-gross assumption has since been exceeded.

rows.companies: Walt Disney Pictures, Seven Bucks Productions, Flynn Picture Company

rows.title: The Bride!

report.basis: Loss could approach $90 million in the first cycle, after home entertainment revenue.
report.assumption: Published after a $13.6 million worldwide opening. No final worldwide gross assumption is specified in the report.
report.caveat: The $90 million is approximate, not an audited final loss.
report.summary: Approximate first-cycle loss after home-entertainment income.

rows.companies: Warner Bros., First Love Films, In the Current Company
